Rulebook and decisions.

Every rule, decision, exception and open item of Edition 04. Generated from brand-rules.md. Decided rules and tokens win; the designer's Figma is the source only for what is not decided yet (R-01).

DecisionsRulesExceptions logOpen items (To confirm)

Rule marks: same unchanged since Edition 02 · changed rewritten for unifiedmeds · new added in Edition 03 or later.

Brand Edition 04 · from 18.11.2026 (the hub merge) · Owner: Avi · Status: APPROVED by Avi · Open items O-01, O-02, O-10, O-12, O-14 and O-17 stay To confirm

Edition 04 opened when the two hubs became one (U-31). Edition 03 (15.11.2026) was the first unifiedmeds edition. Rule IDs R-01 to R-83 keep their earlier numbers so every change can be traced; new rules start at R-84. Earlier editions are archived, never deleted.

Status words: Current (decided, build it) · Phase 2 (designed, ships after launch) · To confirm (open item, never ships as decided) · Retired (no longer applies).

Change marks: same unchanged since Edition 02 · changed rewritten for unifiedmeds (Edition 03 or later) · new added in Edition 03 or later.

Rules.

Authority

  • R-01 changed Decided rules and tokens win. The designer's Figma files (website h7D0eRszARBaWdJT1NWrpZ, logo VX5oKsl1ZIKbiWLR0tjf7L, questionnaire jbfsCm7lPwOgNomoe6J0U3) are read only and are the source only for what is not decided yet. Our own Figma files (design system VqxGNn81aTddK6TOSeum3W, website working copy xGhWMkPtx0zxNzLmThVY4o, questionnaire copy 2M1MM0DPHf9hmJxBlfzld7) are kept in sync with the rules and tokens. A difference between a rule and any Figma file is reported, never copied silently. · Source: U-31
  • R-02 changed brand-rules.md holds every rule and wins on compliance and wording. The hub explains the rules and never adds one of its own; process rules live in the numbered Process section (R-121 to R-129). · Source: U-31
  • R-03 same Every value has one home: tokens/tokens.json. brand.css is generated from it and never edited by hand. No colour, size or duration outside the tokens.
  • R-04 changed This is Brand Edition 04, opened at the hub merge on 18.11.2026 (U-31). Edition 03 (15.11.2026) was the first unifiedmeds edition. The former brand's editions are archived, never deleted and never linked as current.

Brand and naming

  • R-05 changed unifiedmeds is a men's health telehealth brand that launches with Sexual health. Vibe: masculine, on the gentle side. · Source: U-04
  • R-06 changed Launch catalogue: Tadalafil, Sildenafil and Combo (confirmed by Avi 17.11.2026, U-21). Longevity and Hair loss are Phase 2 categories (designed in Figma, not linked as live at launch). Some future products will be for women (Planned). · Source: U-04, U-05
  • R-07 changed The name is unifiedmeds everywhere, all lowercase, also at the start of a sentence. Never "Unifiedmeds", "UnifiedMeds", "Unified Meds" or "UNIFIEDMEDS", and never the former brand name. The legal entity name is To confirm; until then no entity name appears in new material, and the former company name never appears. · Source: U-01, U-07, U-31
  • R-08 same The category is "Sexual health" in navigation and on the category page. "Better Intimacy" is used only as the editorial hero title.
  • R-108 new Product names say what the product is. A single medicine is named by the medicine, then strength and form ("Tadalafil, 20 mg tablets"). A combination gets a short descriptive name ("Combo") with its ingredients written under it. Never a reference brand ("Generic Cialis", "like Viagra"), never a word of result or speed, anatomy or the condition. "UM" is never a short name for the company. In running text a generic name is lower case mid-sentence (tadalafil); on labels the strength follows R-89 (20 mg · Tablets). Product names never appear in email subjects, previews, push notifications or on the mailer. New names follow the naming process on the Brand architecture page (brief, long list, screen, trademark and FDA check, legal, Avi decides). · Source: U-21
  • R-09 same A tagline sits under the name. Until Avi chooses one, no tagline ships. To confirm

  • R-15 changed Coral #E76F51 marks errors and out-of-range results only, always with an icon, never as a text colour. Clay #CFC6B8 is for posters only, never website UI. Packaging follows R-89. · Source: Figma 2678:2
  • R-16 same Pastel Green #6A8670 is for shapes, in-range markers and icons. Never text.

Tokens --color-product-*. On the website (Avi, 17.11.2026, U-28) a product colour also marks its product wherever it is relevant: the product card, the product page accents, the product chip in menus and the recommendation. It marks with a dot or an edge, never carries text or data (use the text colours) and never replaces the category colour of the page (R-117). · Source: U-13, U-14, U-28

Type

It is drawn in Outfit Medium (from the logo sting source; confirmed by Avi 15.11.2026). Outfit is never used for website text.
  • R-19 same The hub copies Figma's text styles 1:1. No size outside the scale.
  • R-20 same Hero: 70/60 on the homepage only, 46/54 on every other page, mobile 34/40. Checked in Figma 15.11.2026: homepage 70/60, Sexual health 46.
  • R-21 same Serif floor: DM Serif never below 24px on desktop or 21px on mobile.
  • R-22 same Labels are sentence case, Inter SemiBold 12/16 +2% (mobile 11/16). No uppercase labels.
  • R-23 same No serif-italic highlight. Avi may re-open it.
  • R-24 same Sentence case for every heading, label, button and nav item. Section headlines end with a full stop and are never questions.
  • R-25 changed Assessment questions are DM Serif 26/1.3 on desktop and on mobile alike (Avi, 18.11.2026), and may be questions. · Source: U-31

Layout

  • R-26 same Frames 1440 desktop and 390 mobile. Content max 1240. Side margins 100 desktop, 40 tablet, 20 mobile.
  • R-27 same 12 columns, 20px gutter. Breakpoints 390 / 768 / 1024 / 1440.
  • R-28 changed Spacing scale only: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 72, 96. Section padding is set by R-116 (64 desktop and tablet, 48 mobile); the earlier 96 / 56 is replaced.
  • R-29 changed Header 80px desktop, 64px mobile, desktop inset 56. Paper, sticky. A 1px Line/Soft border appears after 8px of scroll. The assessment top bar keeps the same heights, 80 desktop and 64 mobile, on Paper, with the progress capsule in the content. · Source: U-31, U-32
  • R-116 new Folds are compact: a section has 64px padding top and bottom on desktop and tablet, 48 on mobile (--layout-section-y, --layout-section-y-mobile); its head sits 24px above its content on desktop, 16 on mobile. Cards keep their own padding; a section head never touches the section above. · Source: U-25
  • R-119 new Two dark bands never touch. A light band (Paper or Mist) always sits between two dark sections: Deep Teal, a dark category colour, a dark CTA band or a dark photo band. On mobile, where sections stack, the same holds. · Source: U-30

Shape and imagery

  • R-30 changed Radius: buttons 5 (--radius-button); cards 16; fields, chips and the dropdown panel 12; menu rows and thumbnails 8; checkboxes 5, like buttons; chips, nav pills and status pills 999 (--radius-pill). No other radius. A checkbox is 22px with a 1.5px Line/Field border (components.css .check). The capsule is a shape (R-31), not a radius value. · Source: U-11, Figma 2676:310
  • R-31 changed Two shape families. Quadrant Kit: Square, Quarter, Half, Circle, Arch, Arc. Capsule: the logo's capsule form, in the variants Split, Split Blue, Outline and Vertical (Figma "Capsule Kit", 2678:2), plus the capsule as an image crop. Both families may appear on the website, as needed. No oval and no soft-cornered rectangle. The capsule shape files are one set in website colours: assets/shapes/capsule-{outline,split,solid}-{h,v}.svg plus capsule-loader.svg; the Sky / Logo Blue set is archived (R-84). · Source: U-03, U-31
  • R-32 changed A capsule may be filled, outline or transparent, and may be shown whole or cropped by the frame edge. Website pattern (Figma homepage, Avi 15.11.2026): a large outline capsule in Wash Blue at 70% opacity (--opacity-capsule), cropped by a section edge; vertical in dark sections; filled capsules at 50% (--opacity-capsule-soft). Quadrant pieces stay axis-aligned and may rotate only during their entrance. How many shapes per surface: R-106. The stroke follows R-109: it scales with the length, never a fixed width. · Source: U-03, Figma 2673:209
  • R-33 changed No text on a shape, ever. A disclaimer never sits on a shape. A photo may be cropped to a capsule.
  • R-105 new Every drawn capsule has the logo's proportions; it is never symmetric. The left half is longer (55% of the full length) and the right half is taller (the left half is 93.3% of its height), measured from assets/brand/logo-seal.svg. A standing capsule is the same shape turned 90° clockwise, long half on top. This applies to every capsule that stands for the logo or the Capsule Kit: split, outline, filled, cropped decor, bands, loaders, icons, illustrations, packaging art, motion and "don't" examples. Draw it only with tools/capsule_svg.py (SVG) or the .um-cap masks from assets/shapes/ (outline and split, at 176px length or more); never a rounded rectangle, border-radius: 999px or roundRect, and size it by one side only so the ratio cannot stretch. Generic UI pills (chips, status, toggles) are not the capsule and keep R-30. · Source: U-22
  • R-106 new Two shapes per surface at most (a slide, a post, a section, a card, an ad): any mix of Capsule and Quadrant Kit pieces counts. A cropped repeat of the same capsule counts as one. Patterns count as one shape and leave no room for a second. · Source: U-23, closes O-05
  • R-109 new Every capsule keeps the logo's construction at every size, as in the seal: the left (long) half is drawn open toward the joint, the right (short, taller) half is closed by the divider line, and the step shows where the two heights meet. Never one continuous outline without the divider (Avi, 17.11.2026: "like the original logo"). The stroke scales with the length: 0.85% of the full length, never under 1.5px (--size-capsule-stroke-ratio, --size-capsule-stroke-min). A filled long half sits inside the outline with a gap, like the seal's filled half. A large capsule that needs weight takes a fill, never a thicker stroke. The stroke applies as rendered to icons, spots and patterns (U-31): spots have one file per size (160 and 96), patterns are used at 1x. Draw it with tools/capsule_svg.py (capsule_paths(), svg_outline(), stroke_for()) or the .um-cap masks from assets/shapes/ (outline and split, at 176px length or more). A fully filled capsule keeps a thin gap at the divider (one stroke wide), like the seal. · Source: U-25, U-26, U-28, U-31
  • R-110 new On a photo the capsule is an outline (R-109), Paper on dark or busy photos and Deep Teal on light ones, with its long half filled translucent (Paper or Wash Blue at --opacity-capsule-soft). It enters from a frame edge or corner, cropped by it, toward the subject; never over a face, eyes or mouth, never under text, never an opaque fill. At most two shapes per photo, the logo icon included (R-106). The logo icon stamp is the u|m mark from the app icon without its tile (assets/shapes/logo-stamp-paper.svg, logo-stamp-teal.svg), long side 48px on desktop and 40 on mobile, 16px from the edges; in exported images 12% of the short side, set 1.5% of the short side from the edges (16px on 1080). On mobile the shape scales with the photo; if the crop would put it over a face it moves to another edge or hides. · Source: U-25
  • R-111 new A fold (section) carries up to two shapes (R-106): the true capsule or Quadrant Kit pieces, outline or translucent fill (--opacity-capsule, --opacity-capsule-soft), never under text. A shape may straddle the boundary between two folds, creating continuity down the page; it counts once in each fold. Optional scroll-linked motion: drift at most 24px (--motion-distance-drift) or turn at most 6° (--motion-drift-rotate), or draw the outline once. Only shapes move, never text. Reduced motion: the end state, static. This extends R-53 and R-104 to every page. · Source: U-25
  • R-34 changed Logo: see R-90 to R-94. The former brand's quadrant symbol is Retired and kept only in the archive.
  • R-35 changed Icons: the unifiedmeds line set built on the capsule (12 feature icons, Figma 3042:221): 1.5px stroke, round caps, no fill, drawn on a 64px grid. Icons are Deep Teal, never Navy and never Yellow; on Deep Teal grounds only the container variant or a Paper line (U-27). The capsule icon family (assets/icons-capsule/, lying and standing) is the website's working set for rows, cards and menus; the feature icons stay for larger moments. Placed sizes: capsule icons 48×24 and 40×20 lying, 64 and 48 standing; feature icons 64 and 48; UI glyphs (assets/icons/ui/) are drawn on a 20 grid at 1.75 and placed at 20, or 24 in icon-only controls. The 1.5px floor applies to the line as rendered: one exported file per placed size (assets/icons/sized/, assets/icons-capsule/sized/), never a scaled file (U-31). The only open point is A or B per subject. · Source: Figma 3042:221, U-27, U-31
  • R-36 same The UI is flat, with borders. One shadow, for dropdowns and dialogs only.
  • R-37 changed Photography: men aged 35 to 65 lead the brand's hero and product imagery. Partners may appear in sexual-health stories. Service and support sections (care team, delivery, member support) use a balanced, modular mix of people of all genders (Avi, 17.11.2026, U-27). Women lead only in future women's products.
  • R-38 same Closed, branded bottles are allowed. Never loose pills, syringes, lab coats or before/after images. At most one faceless detail crop per page.
  • R-39 changed Watermarked placeholder photos never ship on the website, ads or press. Exception (U-27): inside the hub a watermarked paid preview may stand in, with a small "Buy this image" link and the tag "Not approved · to replace". Free-licence stand-ins (Pexels, Unsplash) are hub-only too, credited: their licences do not cover implied endorsement. Photos of unknown source never appear (U-31). The live site uses a commissioned shoot for the key images (home, the three category heroes, about) and licensed stock with model release and sensitive-use clearance for the rest (U-32, O-13 closed). · Source: U-27, U-31, U-32
  • R-120 new Copy and photos work three ways: beside the photo, on a solid colour panel, or directly on the photo. The panel is Paper, Deep Teal or Mist, radius 8, inset 16. Directly on the photo only on a calm area (a wall, a window, sky, a floor), never across a face, skin or a shape (R-33, R-110). Contrast is measured on the area under the letters at every crop: 4.5:1 under 24px, 3:1 for DM Serif at 24px and up; Teal Deep or Deep Teal on light areas, Paper on dark ones; no scrim, gradient or blur. On a photo a headline and one short line at most, and buttons are Outline Light. On a phone, if the crop loses the calm area, the copy moves below the photo. · Source: U-31

Logo

  • R-90 new The logo is the capsule seal: "unified" (bold) in the filled half of a capsule, "meds" (regular) in the open half. Three lockups: Primary seal (where the brand needs presence), Horizontal (capsule icon + wordmark, the website navigation), Stacked (square spaces). In the header: the Horizontal lockup 52px tall on desktop, the Primary seal 50px tall on mobile (R-103); in the footer the Horizontal lockup 30px desktop and 28px mobile. · Source: Figma 3038:178, VX5o 5:80, Avi 15.11.2026
  • R-91 changed On light grounds (Paper, Mist, Cream) use the main version in Navy. On dark grounds (Deep Teal, Ink, Navy) and on photography use the reversed versions only. The website footer sits on Mist with the main Horizontal lockup (R-48, R-114); the reversed logo appears only on the dark CTA band above it. Cream is a ground for presenting the logo (stings, media kit), never a label ground. · Source: Figma 3038:211, U-27
  • R-92 new Clear space: the height of the "meds" half on every side. Never recolour individual parts, stretch, rotate, redraw or add effects. Use the exported files only.
  • R-93 new App icon and favicon: the "u|m" capsule on a Navy rounded square. Favicon sizes 48, 32 and 16; at 16px the capsule is solid. The favicon never uses the wordmark. The 16px file is assets/brand/favicon-16.svg (tools/capsule_svg.py --favicon). · Source: VX5o 5:144
  • R-94 new The logo file also holds Scrubs green, Clinic sky, Black on white, White on black and Grey versions. Decided 17.11.2026 (U-28): only Black on white and White on black, for technical uses (fax, emboss, stamp, one-colour print); Scrubs green, Clinic sky and Grey are not used. The one-colour files are the exported logo with every colour set to black or to white (assets/media-kit/kit/01-logos/one-colour/).

Components

  • R-40 changed Buttons are rounded rectangles, never pills: radius 5 (--radius-button), one height 50px (--size-control), side padding 24 (--size-button-padding-x), so width = label width + 48. Label Inter Medium 15/20, sentence case. Only logged exceptions differ in height (E-02, E-03). · Source: U-11, Figma 2676:310
  • R-41 changed Button types and hover (Figma 2676:310 and 2719:4438): Dark fills Teal-deep #1C3742 with a Paper label and hovers to Yellow; Outline (Teal-deep border) hovers to Yellow; Light (Paper fill) hovers to Yellow; Outline Light on Deep Teal hovers to Yellow, on photos to Blue-dark; Yellow hovers to Blue-dark with a Paper label. Labels on Yellow and Paper are Deep Teal #264653. On a Yellow, Blue or Wash surface every button hovers to Paper, and Light hovers to Deep Teal. Every button lifts 2px in 150ms ease-out. Figma draws the Yellow hover in Pastel Blue #6E8B97 (Paper label 3.53:1, fails AA); Avi confirmed Blue-dark on 15.11.2026 (R-12, R-72); Figma's Pastel Blue is on the clean-up list. · Source: U-11, O-16
  • R-42 changed Fields: 50px, radius 12, 1px Slate border. A selected answer: single choice fills Deep Teal with Paper text and the Yellow mark; multiple choice keeps its ground and shows a Deep Teal border plus a 1px inset; no scale (U-31). Disabled: 40% of the component's own colours (--opacity-disabled), no hover, aria-disabled, fields included (U-28). Loading uses the capsule loader (R-53). A missing answer follows pattern 2: Continue is always active; tapping it without an answer marks the options in Coral, with the error icon (R-15), and shows "Choose an answer to go on.", which clears on the next change. Continue is disabled only while the step is busy and for E-05. Progress mark: the capsule, in the content under the top bar, never in the header; its label sits beside the capsule, never inside; the row is 44px tall and the fill never shows below 10% of the length. On mobile the whole row is one 44px button that opens the step list; on desktop a step rail lists the steps (U-32). · Source: U-28, U-31, U-32
  • R-130 new The assessment has one step model: Welcome and Email first; then seven steps, About you, Health history, Medications, Your main concern, Preferences, Consent and account, Plan and send (recommendation, checkout, ID, send); then the provider review. Sign-in is by email link, never a password. The Notify me page (a state not served, E-05) carries a consent line, an unticked box and double opt-in (U-28). Questions are built from one template with variants and the flow is written as data, so order, screens and question types can change (U-32). · Source: U-28, U-32
  • R-43 same Cards: radius 16. Cards that are links fill Deep Teal with light text on hover, with no lift.
  • R-44 same Step numbers: on hover or tap the circle fills Yellow with dark digits.
  • R-45 changed Launch menu (Figma "short nav" 2738:2783, mobile 2743:3337): Sexual health ▾ · How it works · FAQ · Sign in · Get started. The dropdown lists Tadalafil, Sildenafil and Combo by name only, with no line under the name (U-31), and "View all Sexual health". · Source: U-04, U-05, U-31
  • R-86 new Phase 2 menu (Figma "full nav" 2641:14411, dropdowns 2791:5681 to 2791:5709): adds Longevity and Hair loss, plus a Help dropdown. Its labels follow R-08 and R-24 (sentence case, "Sexual health" not "Better Intimacy"); the final wording is To confirm before Phase 2. · Source: U-04
  • R-46 same Menu behaviour: hover shows a Line/Soft pill (150ms). The dropdown opens on hover after a 100ms intent delay, or on click, Enter or ↓. One dropdown at a time. Esc closes it and returns focus.
  • R-47 same Mobile menu: ☰ in a 44×44 target opens a full-screen menu and locks body scroll. The bottom bar holds Get started and "Assessment only. Not a diagnosis."

Updated 17.11.2026 (U-27, R-114): the footer sits on Mist with the Horizontal logo and a Dark Subscribe button (components.css .ft3); the CTA band above it keeps its dark ground (the category colour on a category page, R-117).
  • R-98 new Alignment: elements in one row share one height; the action (button or link) sits at the bottom of every card on one line across the row; captions sit on one line; image galleries use one frame ratio per row. · Source: U-17
  • R-99 new Button states: Default, Hover, Pressed (hover colours, no lift), Focus (hover look plus the 2px ring), Disabled (40% of the component's own colours, R-42, approved U-28). Loading is the capsule loader. Mobile has no hover: a tap shows Pressed. Same spec on desktop and mobile: Inter Medium 15/20, height 50, padding 24, radius 5, border 1.5 inside; exceptions Header 44 and Mobile bar 48; tap target at least 44. · Source: U-18, U-28
  • R-100 new Buttons with an icon are a second family, never a replacement: same types, colours and states; one 20px icon on the right of the label, in the label colour, 8px gap, padding 24 on the label side and 20 on the icon side. The icon never replaces the label and is never Yellow. On hover the icon moves 2px in its direction (none with reduced motion). · Source: U-18
  • R-112 new Two buttons side by side never show the same colour, at rest or on hover, press or focus. Next to a Yellow button, Outline, Outline Light and Light hover to Deep Teal with a Paper label, and Dark hovers to Blue-dark; on a Deep Teal surface they hover to Paper with a Deep Teal label (components.css, any two buttons sharing a parent; .btn-pair stacks them full width on mobile). An icon-only pager pair is exempt. · Source: U-25
  • R-113 new Interactive states. A toggle's thumb slides between options in 220ms (--motion-duration-open); dependent content cross-fades in 180ms (--motion-duration-crossfade). A two-state control that marks data uses Green for the first state and Blue for the second (Daily Green, As needed Blue), never product colours or Yellow; the dose dots in the member portal follow it too (U-31); marks fill 40ms apart (--motion-stagger-fine). A stepper or scroll story fades steps not reached to 0.45 (--opacity-step-faded), marks the active step with a 2px Deep Teal border, a filled number and a left accent bar, and checks passed steps. An accordion opens one answer at a time; height and opacity animate in 220ms and the chevron turns 180°. Reduced motion: instant, same colours. · Source: U-25, U-31

A licensed provider reviews every assessment.", link columns (Care, Company, Help, Legal) from the landing-page list, without Hair loss, Longevity and Reviews until they launch, with the legal pages named "Terms of service" and "Telehealth notice" (final wording with legal), the newsletter signup (email field, Dark button, consent line, "No product names in our emails"), six social icons in 44px targets (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, X; the platforms' official marks in production), the support contact, the compliance lines ("Assessment only. Not a diagnosis.", telehealth notice, LegitScript seal) and the copyright line. On mobile the newsletter comes first and the columns become a one-open accordion (R-113) with 44px rows. Reference: components.css .ft3. · Source: U-25, U-31
  • R-115 new A section may add one brand accent, Green or Blue, through an icon, an eyebrow mark, a rule or a low-opacity shape of the same hue. One accent per section. Green and Blue mark, they never carry small text. Yellow stays the single result moment (R-11). · Source: U-25
  • R-117 new Each category page carries its category colour, the same as its label ground (R-96): Sexual health Deep Teal (--color-category-sexual-health), Longevity Forest (--color-category-longevity), Hair loss Sky (--color-category-hair-loss, a light ground: text, icons and buttons on it in Deep Teal). The category's dark anchor sections, hero band and category accents (eyebrow, tags, the category card on the home gateway, the menu marker) use it; Paper text on Deep Teal and Forest; AA contrast. Yellow stays the single result moment. Product colours mark their product with a dot or an edge, never carry text or data, and never replace the category colour (R-85, U-28). · Source: U-27, U-28

Motion

  • R-49 same One principle: "Motion confirms, it never performs."
  • R-50 changed Durations: 150 hover, press, select, focus · 180 crossfade · 220 open, close, slide, accordion, step · 320 reveal · 420 wipe · 520 shape · 1400 loader. Staggers 90 (three items at most) and 40 (marks, within 180). No other duration. Delays are not durations and come from the tokens only: 100 menu intent, 150 before a menu closes, 400 before a loader shows, 320 before the assessment advances.
  • R-51 same Easing: ease-out for every UI transition; the enter curve only for brand shapes entering.
  • R-52 same Brand moves: Rise 12px; Pivot 520ms, no fade; Wipe 420ms; stagger 90ms, three items at most; Count for results only.
  • R-53 changed Nothing loops on the website except the capsule loader (1.4s, R-42, M-023). Hero: static copy plus one shape entrance.
  • R-54 changed The hub's motion page is the only motion reference: the motion cards (M-001 to M-024), logo motion and the stings (R-101), landing-page moments (R-104), fold drift (R-111) and interactive states (R-113). Videos has its own page.
  • R-101 new Logo stings: B is the default, C1 for brand and story moments, C2 for short social openers. One sting per video, at the start or the end, never in the middle. All three stings end on the seal on Cream (color.logo.cream), as in the files (R-91, U-31). · Source: U-12, U-31
  • R-104 new Landing pages (campaign pages outside the website menu) may carry up to three brand moments: a capsule that draws, fills, closes or slides in. Each plays once, never loops, and uses the motion tokens only (R-50 to R-52). Where it tells a sequence, it follows the scroll, so the visitor sets the pace. One photo parallax at most, desktop only, at 0.85x. Rise on enter (12px, three items at most) is not a brand moment. The hero copy stays readable from the first frame: only the shape moves (R-53). With reduced motion every moment is off and the page shows its end state. The website itself keeps R-53. · Source: U-20, Sexual health landing page 16.11.2026

Content

  • R-55 changed The primary CTA is "Get started", in sentence case everywhere. The action on a product or category card is "Learn more" (U-31).
  • R-56 same US English. Plain, short sentences in the active voice.
  • R-57 changed Glossary: provider (not doctor or clinician), assessment (not quiz, visit or online visit), member (not patient). Confirmed by Avi 17.11.2026 (U-27): "online visit" is replaced by "assessment" everywhere, the landing page included. "Care team" means the provider and the support team together; it is used in messages and in print (U-31). Exception: the pharmacy leaflet keeps "patient". · Source: U-27, U-31
  • R-58 same A hero headline and subhead carry no benefit claim, price or symptom list.
  • R-59 same At most one normalising line per page, with no numbers.
  • R-60 same A number never appears bare: it carries its unit and, for results, its range. One assessment length everywhere; until it is set, every place shows the placeholder "[about N minutes · O-12]". To confirm
  • R-61 same No prices in heroes. Savings as a dollar amount per product, never a blanket "Save 15%".
  • R-62 changed One charge line everywhere. Until operations decides it, every place shows the placeholder "[charge line · operations]": no consultation price and no "only charged if a provider approves" (Avi, 18.11.2026). It sits in a hero under the button, never in the headline or subhead (R-61); next to the assessment CTA on category, product and landing pages; in the plan card and at checkout; the FAQ quotes it. The wording is To confirm (O-12). · Source: U-31

Compliance and privacy

  • R-63 changed "Assessment only. Not a diagnosis." next to every assessment CTA above the fold, in the mobile menu bottom bar and in every assessment screen footer, with the emergency line. Visible on load. In an ad it sits inside the art or on the video end card, never only in the caption; an organic post that links to the assessment carries it in the caption.
  • R-64 same Wherever a next step is offered, a licensed provider is named as responsible for it.
  • R-65 changed Rx product names may appear in navigation and on product pages that carry safety information. Never in heroes or ads, and never next to a benefit claim. The product page title (the name alone, DM Serif 46 at most, 34 on mobile) is not a hero; no claim, price or benefit sits beside it.
  • R-87 new Longevity and Hair loss product pages (NAD+ Capsules, NAD+ injection, Metformin, Finasteride, Hair Growth Spray) carry the status Legal review required and do not ship until legal approves them. This replaces the earlier decision to remove drug names from Longevity. · Source: U-06
  • R-66 same Safety information on a product page is always fully expanded.
  • R-67 changed No press strip, clinical statistics, success rates, reviews, testimonials, endorsements, certifications or star ratings until legal approves real data. Until then a prototype may show a review only in the prototype format: the DEMO ONLY marker, the attribution "Member · age", never "Verified" and never a star rating. The Sexual health landing page keeps its review section in that format (Avi, 18.11.2026). · Source: U-31
  • R-68 same No promised review or shipping time until operations confirm a service level.
  • R-69 same Illustrative medical content shows the DEMO ONLY notice. Never invent clinical rules or statistics.
  • R-70 same Assessment answers are collected only on the clinical intake domain.
  • R-71 changed No tracking pixels, ad tags or session replay on condition or product pages. Consent comes before any analytics, first-party assessment events included: nothing runs until the visitor agrees, and assessment events carry screen IDs only. Legal may approve an exception in writing (q137). · Source: U-31
  • R-88 new Footer legal line: "© 2026 unifiedmeds". Entity name, domain and contact email are added when confirmed. · Source: U-07

Accessibility

  • R-72 to R-77 same WCAG AA contrast, 2px Deep Teal focus ring (Paper on dark), 44×44 tap targets, hover also works with touch and keyboard, reduced motion is instant, no sideways scroll at 390px.
  • R-95 new The logo colours meet contrast in the versions in R-91. Any new logo pairing is checked for 3:1 before use.
  • R-102 new Every page of the hub carries <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">: open to anyone with the link, never listed by search engines. · Source: U-15

Process

  • R-78 to R-82 same A rule changes in this order: decision → brand-rules.md → tokens → changelog → release. No silent mismatches. Exceptions are logged before they ship. Open items are marked To confirm.
  • R-83 changed Edition 04 opened at the hub merge (18.11.2026). Later changes are dated updates of Edition 04 in the changelog; only replacing the palette or the type scale opens a new edition. · Source: U-31
  • R-107 new Mobile gets equal treatment. Every category, deliverable and element in the hub shows and documents its mobile version wherever it differs from desktop: layout and grid, type sizes, line breaks, what stacks or hides, sizes and safe zones, tap targets (44px minimum) and technical notes. Every page is checked at 1440 and 390 wide before it ships: no sideways scroll, nothing cut off. · Source: U-24
  • R-121 new Who approves what. Every asset has at least one approver who can stop it. Brand (Avi) gives the final sign-off on everything except medicine claims and safety text, which belong to the clinical team and legal. A clinical or legal no stops an asset; brand cannot overrule it and makes the asked change in the brand's own way. The approval matrix per asset type lives on How we work. The approvers' names, and who approves medical content, are To confirm (O-17). · Source: U-30
  • R-122 new Legal approves every social post at launch, after the brand check and before the final sign-off. Medical content always adds the clinical step: any line about a condition, a symptom, a medicine, safety, side effects or results counts, and when in doubt it counts. · Source: U-30
  • R-123 new Two change paths. A rule or a value changes by R-78 to R-83. An asset ships by the approval flow: draft → brand check → clinical (only with medical content) → legal → final sign-off → publish → log. Before publishing, the one coded pre-publish checklist (Brand B, Compliance C, Accessibility A, Discretion D, Tracking T, Filing F, plus the developer rows for website builds) runs on the exact file that ships, at 1440 and 390 wide (R-107); website builds are also checked at 768 and 1024. · Source: U-30, U-31
  • R-124 new Files live in a Google Shared Drive, so they belong to the company, not to one person: one numbered folder per channel, the same four stages inside each (1-work, 2-review, 3-approved, 9-archive). On approval a file moves from 1-work to 3-approved with its name unchanged and no suffix; the channel owner publishes it unchanged from there. An approved file is never edited: a change starts the next version in 1-work. · Source: U-30
  • R-125 new The approval log is a sheet in the Drive's 00-admin folder. Every published file gets one row: ID, file name, who approved it and when, the checklist codes that were run, where and when it was published, and the version it replaces. · Source: U-30
  • R-126 new File names have eight fields, in this order, always all eight: um_channel_asset_product-or-category_variant_size_vNN_yyyymmdd.ext. Lowercase letters and numbers only; hyphens inside a field, underscores between fields; never "final", "new", "latest" or "copy". Status lives in the folder, never in the name. Every change that is shared again gets the next version number (v01 is the first version anyone else sees). The convention covers the Drive, every export and every file sent outside the team; code and the hub keep their own short names. Figma names use " · " as the separator and carry no status or version. · Source: U-30
  • R-127 new Archive, never delete. A replaced or retired file moves with its name unchanged: to 9-archive in its channel folder, a whole retired edition to 99-archive, and inside the hub to archive/ with its relative path kept. The log records the move and what replaced it. Nothing in an archive is linked as current from a live page, the hub or a template. Emptying a trash is Avi's call only. · Source: U-16, U-30
  • R-128 new Data in the member portal. Dose marking at launch is a reminder from the plan with an optional check he can tap: no streaks, scores, grades, badges or confetti. Yellow marks only the next step on a timeline, once per screen, never a series, a band or a tile (R-11). The first series is Deep Teal and the second Pastel Blue, two series at most, each with a direct label and its own marker shape, so colour is never the only key. Big figures are Inter SemiBold, never DM Serif. Two-state dose dots follow R-113. · Source: U-30, U-31
  • R-129 new Wrong examples stay. A "don't" example in the hub may show real condition words (for example "ED") or claim language, because it is always clearly marked Wrong, with the rule it breaks. A Wrong example never leaves its marked card and is never reused as copy. · Source: U-30
